text:
The Flyers snapped a three-game winless run (0-2-1) on Sunday, and they did it by winning a game their opponent played better. PHI beat UTA 6-3 at Xfinity Mobile Arena despite being out-chanced for most of it. Travis Konecny, picked 24th overall by Philadelphia in 2015, scored and added an assist to take first star, with Jamie Drysdale's three assists earning him second.

Our numbers see a different game. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of goals, favored UTA 2.93 to 2.21, and UTA took 55 shot attempts to PHI's 47. In the simulated replays we run of every shot, UTA would have won 64 percent of the time. UTA owned the first period, 1.27 to 0.58, but the Flyers took the second 1.00 to 0.48 and turned it into a lead. Several of their goals came on modest looks: Noah Cates scored on a 5 percent chance, and so did Oliver Bonk in the third. Karel Vejmelka allowed 2.8 more goals than the shots he faced deserved, while Dan Vladar's night was roughly even with what he was asked to stop.

UTA made it interesting late. Mikhail Sergachev and Logan Cooley scored power-play goals 67 seconds apart in the third to cut it to 5-3, but Cole Knuble answered with 94 seconds left to seal it. The Flyers leave with the winless run behind them. UTA, which went 2 for 5 on the power play, takes the loss with it.
